# Use a sandbox through the REST API

## Intent

An agent or a person who has a sandbox must be able to work in it with nothing but the hub's REST API and the `parley` CLI: run commands and read their output, move files in and out, read what the main process and the network policy logged, and open an interactive terminal. No client of the sandbox runtime is needed, a weak credential cannot act through a sandbox that a stronger one created, and the hub knows when a sandbox was last used.

## Goals

- `POST /workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/exec` runs a command and answers with its exit code and its output, collected (up to 1 MiB per stream) or as an event stream without that cap.
- A command that runs longer than its `timeout` is killed and reported with `timed_out: true`; a command whose caller goes away is killed.
- At most `[sandbox].max_concurrent_execs` commands (default 8) run at once in one sandbox; one more is answered `429`.
- `PUT` and `GET /workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/files` move one file or a tar stream, only under the sandbox's working directory, up to `[sandbox].max_transfer_size` (default 1 GiB).
- The hub stores the output of the main process and the runtime's policy log for each sandbox, with exposed secret values replaced by `[redacted]`, keeps the last `[sandbox].log_retention` (default 7 days) and serves it as pages or as a followed stream.
- `GET /workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/attach` gives an interactive terminal over WebSocket on a new shell.
- Exec, attach, file transfer and output of the main process each set the sandbox's `last_activity_at`.
- `parley sandbox exec`, `shell`, `logs`, `upload` and `download` do all of this from a shell, and `parley sandbox exec` exits with the command's exit code.

## Non-goals

- The `[sandbox]` configuration (including `max_exec_timeout`, `max_concurrent_execs`, `max_transfer_size` and `log_retention`), its validation, the start-up runtime check, profiles, the runtime client interface with its fake, the check order of sandbox routes and the no-widening rule itself: package 44 sandbox_runtime_and_profiles. This package reads those values, calls that rule and the runtime-error answer, and calls the runtime client by the operation names that package declares, adding none.
- The sandbox record, its state machine, creation, credentials, exposed secrets and their resolution, the checkout, and `parley sandbox create|list|get`: package 45 sandbox_creation_and_credentials.
- Stop, start, idle stop (which reads the `last_activity_at` this package writes), expiry, delete, checkpoints, reconciliation, the removal of `deleted` records after 24 hours and hub shutdown: package 47 sandbox_lifecycle_and_checkpoints. When it removes a record it runs the purge hooks of package 45, through which this package removes the sandbox's stored lines.
- Denial events (`parley.sandbox.deny`), proposals and workspace sandbox rules: package 48 sandbox_network_policy. This package only stores the policy log lines and serves them.
- The telemetry record of sandbox use (`sandbox.exec`, `sandbox.attach`, `sandbox.upload`, `sandbox.download`, AUD-FR-026): package 50 telemetry_ingestion. This package offers the observer registry that record is written from; `parleyd` registers the recorder of package 50 with it where that package exists.
- The metric catalogue and `/metrics`: package 51 audit_query_and_retention. This package reports `parley_sandbox_exec_total{result}` to the metrics recorder that package 44 declares.
- The error envelope, list paging, body limits and the check order of every route: package 02 http_api_conventions. The CLI's settings, output and exit codes: package 09 cli_foundation.
- Hub events: exec, attach, file transfer and log reads emit none (§13.8).
- Redaction of exec output, the exec stream, the attach terminal and downloaded files: the source PRD excludes it (SBX-FR-068).
- Following symbolic links inside the sandbox when a path is resolved (design decision 9).

## Background

The repository holds no code yet; every file named here is new. Package 44 puts the runtime client interface over the OpenShell SDK, its fake for tests and the no-widening rule in `internal/sandbox/`. Package 45 adds the sandbox record (with `state`, `hub_access`, `last_activity_at`, the fixed working directory `/workspace` and the environment of the sandbox), the scrubbing function for a sandbox's secret values and the purge hooks and its routes in the same directory, and the first `parley sandbox` commands in `internal/cli/sandbox.go`. This package adds the routes that use a sandbox, in `internal/sandbox/`, and five commands to `internal/cli/sandbox.go`, built on the client of `internal/cli/` (package 09).

The source is `docs/prd/13_sandboxes.md`: SBX-FR-030 to SBX-FR-036, the routes `exec`, `files`, `logs` and `attach` of §13.5, the commands `exec`, `shell`, `logs`, `upload` and `download` of §13.6, and the edge cases of §13.10 that concern them.

## Requirements

All routes are under `/api/v1` and follow the conventions of §3 (PLAT-FR-010 to PLAT-FR-019).

### Who may use a sandbox, and when (SBX-FR-010 to SBX-FR-012, §13.3.3)

Five routes are covered, all under `/workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id`: `POST …/exec` (collected and streamed), `PUT …/files`, `GET …/files`, `GET …/logs` and `GET …/attach`.

Every request passes the checks in this order; the first failing one decides the answer:

1. steps 1 to 4 of the global order (path and method, authentication, rate limit, body size and content type);
2. sandboxes enabled, else `404`, `error_type` `sandboxes_disabled`;
3. the binding guard for bound tokens (package 08);
4. PAT scope: `sandboxes:read` for `GET …/files` and `GET …/logs`, `sandboxes:write` for exec, `PUT …/files` and attach; else `403 insufficient_scope`;
5. workspace access: read for the two read routes, write for the others; a workspace the caller cannot see is `404 not_found`; a read-only member on a write route is `403 forbidden`;
6. the sandbox: an id that is unknown, belongs to another workspace, or whose record was removed is `404`, `error_type` `sandbox_not_found`;
7. no widening (SBX-FR-012), for exec, attach and `PUT …/files` only: the caller's credential must cover the sandbox's hub credential, else `403 insufficient_scope`. Download and logs are not subject to it;
8. validation of the request, `400`;
9. state, `409`, `error_type` `sandbox_not_ready`:

   | Route | Allowed states |
   |---|---|
   | exec, attach, `PUT …/files` | `ready` |
   | `GET …/files` | `ready`, `completed`, `failed` |
   | `GET …/logs` | every state, `deleted` included, while the record exists |

When the runtime cannot be reached or fails while it serves exec, a file transfer or attach, the answer is the runtime-error answer of package 44: `502`, `error_type` `sandbox_runtime_error`, with the runtime's text scrubbed of the sandbox's secret values and cut to 1,024 bytes as its message (SBX-FR-064). Logs are served from the hub's own store and do not need the runtime.

### Exec, collected (SBX-FR-030, SBX-FR-032)

`POST /workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/exec` with body `{"command": string[], "workdir"?: string, "env"?: map, "stdin"?: string, "stdin_base64"?: string, "timeout"?: duration}`.

The command runs in the sandbox as the workload user, in the sandbox's working directory unless `workdir` names another directory, with the sandbox's environment plus the request's `env`. `stdin`, when given, is written to the command's standard input, which is then closed. Exec is independent of the main process: it is accepted whether or not a main process runs.

The request waits for the command. The answer is `200`:

```json
{"exit_code": 0, "stdout": "…", "stderr": "…", "truncated": false, "timed_out": false, "duration_ms": 12}
```

- A non-zero exit code is not an error: the answer is `200` with that `exit_code`.
- **Timeout.** `timeout` defaults to 60 s. When the command still runs after it, the hub kills the command and answers `200` with `timed_out: true`, `exit_code: null` and the output collected until then.
- **Output cap.** At most 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes) of each of stdout and stderr is returned. More is dropped, and `truncated` is `true` when either stream lost bytes.
- **Output that is not UTF-8.** A stream whose returned bytes are not valid UTF-8 is returned in `stdout_base64` or `stderr_base64`, and its text member is `""`. The `_base64` member is absent otherwise.
- **The caller disconnects.** The command is killed (§13.10).

Refusals:

- `400 invalid_request`: `command` absent, empty, not a list of strings, or longer than 256 entries; `env` with more than 64 entries, a value over 8 KiB, a name starting with `PARLEY_` or `OPENSHELL_`, or a name the sandbox's `exposed_secrets` lists (SBX-FR-066); both `stdin` and `stdin_base64`; `stdin_base64` that is not base64; stdin over 4 MiB (4,194,304 bytes) after decoding; `timeout` that is not a duration, is zero, or exceeds `[sandbox].max_exec_timeout` (default 30 min).
- `413 payload_too_large`: a body over 8 MiB.
- `429 rate_limited`: `[sandbox].max_concurrent_execs` (default 8) commands already run in this sandbox through exec. The count covers collected and streamed execs of one sandbox and nothing else. A command that ended for any reason no longer counts.
- `502 sandbox_runtime_error`: the runtime could not run the command.

### Exec, streamed (SBX-FR-031)

The same request with an `Accept` header that names `text/event-stream` is answered `200` with `Content-Type: text/event-stream`:

- frames `event: stdout` and `event: stderr`, each with data `{"data": string}` or, for a chunk that is not valid UTF-8, `{"data_base64": string}`; a frame carries at most 32 KiB of output;
- one final frame `event: exit` with data `{"exit_code", "timed_out", "duration_ms"}`, after which the hub closes the stream.

There is no 1 MiB cap: every byte of output is delivered. The timeout applies as for the collected form and ends the stream with `timed_out: true`, `exit_code: null`. Closing the stream kills the command. Every refusal of the collected form is answered the same way here, as a JSON error envelope and not as a stream, because it is decided before the command starts. A runtime failure after the stream began ends the stream without an `exit` frame.

### Files (SBX-FR-033)

**Upload.** `PUT /workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/files?path=…[&archive=tar][&mode=…]`, body `application/octet-stream` (with `archive=tar`, `application/x-tar` is accepted too).

- Without `archive`, the body becomes the content of the file at `path`. Missing parent directories are created, an existing file is replaced, and the file gets `mode` (octal, `0000` to `0777`; default `0644`).
- With `archive=tar`, the body is a tar stream that is unpacked under the directory `path`, which is created when missing. Regular files and directories are written with the modes of their entries.
- Answer: `200 {"path", "bytes", "entries"}`: the absolute path, the file bytes written, and the number of files and directories written (1 for a single file).

**Download.** `GET /workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/files?path=…[&archive=tar]`.

- A file is answered `200` with its bytes, `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` and its `Content-Length`.
- With `archive=tar`, the answer is `200` with `Content-Type: application/x-tar`: for a directory, a tar stream of its files and directories with names relative to it; for a file, a tar stream with that one entry.

**Paths.** `path` is absolute or relative to the working directory, which is `/workspace` for every sandbox (package 45). A path that resolves outside the working directory is `400`, `error_type` `path_outside_workdir`, and so is a tar entry whose name resolves outside `path`.

**Limits.** A transfer is streamed and limited to `[sandbox].max_transfer_size` (default 1 GiB), counted over the request body of an upload and over the bytes sent of a download.

Refusals:

- `400 invalid_request`: `path` absent or empty; `archive` other than `tar`; `mode` not octal or given together with `archive=tar`; a tar stream that cannot be read or that holds an entry that is neither a regular file nor a directory.
- `400`, `error_type` `path_is_directory`: a download of a directory without `archive=tar`.
- `404`, `error_type` `path_not_found`: a download of a path that does not exist, or of a sandbox whose working directory the runtime no longer has.
- `413 payload_too_large`: an upload whose declared length exceeds the limit (nothing is written); an upload without a declared length that passes it (the hub stops reading and writing; what was written stays); a download of a file larger than the limit (no byte is sent). A tar download that passes the limit is cut off: the hub aborts the connection, so the caller sees an incomplete transfer.
- `415 unsupported_media_type`: an upload with another content type.
- `502 sandbox_runtime_error`.

### Logs (SBX-FR-034, SBX-FR-068)

**What is stored.** While a sandbox is `ready`, the hub reads from the runtime the output of the main process and the runtime's policy log for the sandbox, and stores each line:

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `time` | when the runtime produced the line |
| `source` | `process` or `policy` |
| `stream` | `stdout` or `stderr` for a process line; `null` for a policy line |
| `line` | the text, without its line end |
| `action`, `program`, `host`, `port` | policy lines only: `allow` or `deny` and what was decided on |
| `credential` | policy lines of credentialed requests only: the provider name |

- Before a line is stored, each exact match of a value of the sandbox's exposed secrets is replaced by `[redacted]`. A value shorter than 8 characters is not matched (SBX-FR-068).
- A line longer than 16 KiB is stored as consecutive lines of at most 16 KiB.
- When the hub restarts, or the runtime's stream breaks, collection resumes within 5 seconds after the last stored line; no line is stored twice.
- Collection stops when the sandbox leaves `ready`. Stored lines stay readable.
- The hourly maintenance run removes lines older than `[sandbox].log_retention` (default 7 days) and the lines of sandboxes whose record no longer exists. The lines of a sandbox also go in the transaction that removes its record, through a purge hook.

**Reading.** `GET /workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/logs` answers `200 {"items": […], "next_cursor"}` with the stored lines oldest first, paged by `limit` and `cursor` (PLAT-FR-014). It works in every state of the sandbox and while the runtime is unreachable.

| Query | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `source` | `process` or `policy`; default both |
| `since` | a timestamp; only lines at or after it |
| `tail` | a positive integer; only the last that many matching lines |
| `follow` | `true`: the answer is an event stream |

**Following.** With `follow=true` the answer is `200` with `Content-Type: text/event-stream`: one frame `event: log` per line, its data the line's JSON object; first the stored lines the other parameters select, then each new line as it is stored. The stream ends when the caller closes it, when the hub stops, or when the sandbox becomes `deleted`.

Refusals, all `400 invalid_request`: an unknown `source`; a `since` that is not a timestamp; a `tail` below 1 or not an integer; a `follow` that is not `true` or `false`; `follow=true` together with `cursor` or `limit`.

### Attach (SBX-FR-035)

`GET /workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/attach?cols=…&rows=…` is a WebSocket upgrade. The hub starts a new shell (`/bin/sh`) in the sandbox as the workload user, in the working directory, with the sandbox's environment, on a terminal of `cols` by `rows` (default 80 by 24; each 1 to 1,000).

- Binary frames carry terminal bytes in both directions.
- A text frame `{"resize": {"cols", "rows"}}` from the caller resizes the terminal. Any other text frame is ignored.
- When the caller closes the connection, the hub ends that shell and nothing else: the main process, running execs and other terminals go on.
- When the shell ends, or the runtime's terminal fails, the hub closes the connection.

Every refusal is a plain HTTP error envelope before the upgrade, and no shell is started: the checks above, `400 invalid_request` for a request that is not a WebSocket upgrade or has `cols` or `rows` outside 1 to 1,000, and `502 sandbox_runtime_error` when the runtime cannot open the terminal.

### Activity (SBX-FR-036)

`last_activity_at` of a sandbox is set to the current time:

- when an exec starts and when it ends, in both forms;
- when an attach opens, when it closes, and while it is open whenever a frame arrives from the caller (stored at most once a minute);
- when a file transfer starts and when it ends;
- when a line of main-process output is stored.

It never moves backwards. A running main process that produces no output, a policy log line, a log read and a refused request do not set it.

**Operation observers.** When an exec, an attach or a file transfer that passed every check ends, the hub tells each registered observer once: the kind (`exec`, `attach`, `upload`, `download`), the sandbox id, its workspace and session, the caller (`actor_type`, `actor_id`), the start time and `duration_ms`; for an exec also the `command`, `exit_code`, `timed_out` and the result (`ok`, `nonzero`, `timeout`, `error`); for a transfer the `path` and `bytes`. Never stdin, output, terminal content, file content or environment values. An observer that fails changes nothing for the caller. The recorder of package 50 is registered as an observer; this package registers none. When an exec ends, the hub also adds one to `parley_sandbox_exec_total{result}`.

### CLI (§13.6)

All five commands follow the CLI conventions (PLAT-FR-090 to PLAT-FR-095). None of them uses the 30-second request timeout: each request lasts until the hub ends it.

**`parley sandbox exec <workspace-slug> <id> -- <command...>`.** Flags: `--workdir`, `--env key=value` (repeatable), `--timeout`, `--stdin` (read standard input to its end and send it), `--json`.

- By default it calls `POST …/exec` as a stream and writes the command's stdout to stdout and its stderr to stderr, byte for byte. Stdout is not JSON.
- With `--json` it calls the collected form and prints the response document.
- Exit status: the command's exit code when it ran, with values above 125 mapped to 125; 1 for a hub error or a timeout (reported on stderr as `wait_timeout`); 2 for a usage or client error, which includes no command after `--`, an `--env` value without `=`, standard input over 4 MiB, and a stream that ends without an `exit` frame.

**`parley sandbox shell <workspace-slug> <id>`.** Opens `GET …/attach` with the size of the local terminal (80 by 24 when standard input is not a terminal), puts the local terminal in raw mode, copies bytes both ways, sends a resize frame when the local terminal changes size, and restores the terminal when the connection ends. Exit status 0 when the hub closes the connection; 1 for a hub error before the upgrade; 2 for a connection failure.

**`parley sandbox logs <workspace-slug> <id>`.** Flags: `--source process|policy`, `--since`, `--tail <n>`, `--follow`. Output: one JSON object per line. Without `--follow` it reads every page. With `--follow` it prints lines as they arrive until the hub ends the stream, then exits 0.

**`parley sandbox upload <workspace-slug> <id> <local-path> <sandbox-path>`.** A local file is sent as the body with its permission bits as `mode`; a local directory is sent as a tar stream with `archive=tar` (regular files and directories; a symbolic link is skipped with a warning on stderr). Output: the response document. A local path that cannot be read is a `client_error` (exit status 2) and no request is sent.

**`parley sandbox download <workspace-slug> <id> <sandbox-path> <local-path>`.** Calls `GET …/files`; when the hub answers `path_is_directory` it asks again with `archive=tar` and unpacks the stream into the directory `<local-path>`. A file is written to `<local-path>`, or to stdout when `<local-path>` is `-`. Output otherwise: `{"path": "<local-path>", "bytes": <n>}`. A tar entry that would be written outside `<local-path>` is a `client_error` (exit status 2).

### End-to-end flows

1. An agent with a `ready` sandbox on its fork uploads a script with `PUT …/files`, runs it with `POST …/exec`, and downloads the file the script wrote with `GET …/files`. `parleyd` checks the caller, passes each operation to the OpenShell gateway, and answers with the exit code, the output and the file. The sandbox's `last_activity_at` has moved.
2. A developer runs `parley sandbox exec <fork> <id> -- sh -c 'echo out; echo err >&2; exit 3'`. The CLI asks for a stream; `parleyd` relays the frames from the OpenShell gateway; the CLI prints `out` on stdout and `err` on stderr and exits 3.
3. A sandbox's main process prints a line that contains an exposed secret's value. `parleyd` reads it from the OpenShell gateway, stores it redacted, and a developer running `parley sandbox logs <fork> <id>` gets it as one JSON line with `[redacted]` in place of the value.
4. A developer opens `GET …/attach` over WebSocket, types `echo hi` and reads `hi` back from the shell the OpenShell gateway started; closing the connection ends that shell, and the sandbox stays `ready`.

## Design Decisions

1. **Project decisions relied on.** Go; `net/http` with its method-and-pattern router; the CLI on `github.com/spf13/cobra`; the sandbox runtime client is `github.com/ai-openshell/sdk-go`, reached only through the runtime client interface of package 44; the store is SQLite behind `internal/store`; tests use `testing`, `net/http/httptest` and the fake runtime of package 44; code takes a replaceable clock.
2. **Runtime operations.** This package calls the runtime client of package 44 by that package's names and adds nothing to the interface, its OpenShell implementation or its fake: `ExecStream` (both forms of exec), `Upload` and `MakeDir`, `Stat`, `Download` and `Walk`, `Logs` with the sources `process` and `policy`, and `ExecInteractive`. A result of kind `unsupported` is answered like an unreachable runtime, `502 sandbox_runtime_error`; a `not found` for a path is `404 path_not_found`.
3. **WebSocket library.** `golang.org/x/net/websocket` for the hub and the CLI. Why: the standard library has none, this module is in the module cache and its signatures were read; the route needs only binary and text frames. `golang.org/x/term` gives the CLI raw mode and the terminal size.
4. **Where the no-widening check sits.** After the sandbox is found and before validation and state. Why: the rule needs the sandbox's `hub_access`, and an authorization answer must not depend on the body.
5. **One state error.** Every state that does not allow the operation, `deleted` included, is `409 sandbox_not_ready`. Why: the routes of §13.5 list no other state error.
6. **The `429` of the exec limit** is the generic `rate_limited` without a `Retry-After` header. Why: the source PRD gives the status only, and the limit is a quantity, not a rate. Attach does not count toward it. The count is held in memory: a restart of the hub ends every exec request anyway (SBX-FR-060).
7. **Exec validation.** `command` and `env` follow the rules of the create request (256 entries; 64 entries of at most 8 KiB; reserved and exposed names refused). The request's value wins over the sandbox's for the same name. A `timeout` above the maximum is refused, not lowered. `exit_code` is `null` only when the command timed out. `workdir` is not confined to the working directory: the runtime's filesystem policy confines the command. The exec body limit is 8 MiB, so that 4 MiB of stdin fits as base64.
8. **Truncated text.** A truncated stream is cut back to the last complete UTF-8 character at or below 1 MiB before its validity is judged, so that a cut inside a character does not turn text into base64.
9. **Path resolution is lexical.** The hub cleans `.` and `..` and compares with the working directory. It does not follow symbolic links inside the sandbox; what a path reaches through a link is confined by the runtime. For that reason tar entries that are links or devices are refused on upload.
10. **A failed upload is not rolled back.** What was written before a refused tar entry or before the size limit stays in the sandbox. Why: the transfer is streamed.
11. **`path_is_directory`** (`400`) is a new specific error type. Why: `parley sandbox download` takes no flag that says whether the path is a directory, so the hub must say it in a way a client can act on. `archive=tar` on a file gives a one-entry tar instead of an error.
12. **Runtime errors use the answer of package 44.** That package owns `502 sandbox_runtime_error`; this package returns runtime failures through it and writes no second answer. The message is the runtime's text after the scrubbing function of package 45 replaced the sandbox's resolved secret values and its hub credential and cut it to 1,024 bytes (SBX-FR-064), as package 47 does for its routes.
13. **Log collection finds its sandboxes by looking.** Every 5 seconds the collector reads the sandboxes in state `ready` from the store, starts a follower for each that has none and stops the followers of the others. Why: it needs no hook in packages 45 and 47, and it resumes after a restart by the same rule. A follower asks the runtime for output from the time of the last stored line and skips the lines of that second it already has.
14. **Log line shape.** `time` has whole seconds (PLAT-FR-016); order is the order of storage. `stream` is `null` for policy lines. `tail` selects the last n matching lines and the result is still paged. Lines are capped at 16 KiB.
15. **Follow frames** are named `log`. The followed stream of a sandbox that is not `ready` stays open, because a start may produce new lines; it ends at `deleted`.
16. **Logs go with their record through a purge hook, and by retention.** This package registers a purge hook with the list package 45 declares; package 47, which removes records after 24 hours and with their workspace, runs it in the removing transaction. The maintenance task registered in the registry of package 03 removes lines by age and, as a backstop, lines whose sandbox record is gone. This package does not depend on package 47.
17. **Attach.** The shell is `/bin/sh`. A request that is not a WebSocket upgrade is `400 invalid_request`. A malformed text frame is ignored. Authentication is the `Authorization` header, as on every route.
18. **Activity during long operations.** Exec and transfers set `last_activity_at` at start and at end; attach also on input, at most once a minute. Why: SBX-FR-036 names the operations, not the moments, and an open terminal in use must not be stopped as idle.
19. **Operation observers and the exec metric.** An in-process registry in `internal/sandbox` with a registration function. Why: AUD-FR-026 belongs to package 50, which does not depend on this package; `internal/hub` registers that package's sandbox recorder as an observer, mapping the record's members one to one. The metric `parley_sandbox_exec_total{result}` is reported by this package itself through the metrics recorder interface of package 44, which package 51's recorder fills.
20. **CLI choices.** `--stdin` sends `stdin_base64`. A timed-out command is reported as `wait_timeout` (the CLI's existing type for a passed timeout) with exit status 1. A stream that ends without an `exit` frame is a `client_error`. `parley sandbox logs` without `--follow` reads all pages. `parley sandbox download` writes a file through a temporary file beside the target and prints `{"path", "bytes"}`; `-` sends the bytes to stdout.
21. **Profile: full.**

## Dependencies

- Package 45 sandbox_creation_and_credentials (draft): the sandbox record this package reads (`state`, `hub_access`, `exposed_secrets`, the working directory, the environment, the session) and writes (`last_activity_at`), and the `parley sandbox` command group.
- Package 09 cli_foundation (draft): the HTTP client, output and exit codes the five commands are built on.
- Through package 45: package 44 sandbox_runtime_and_profiles (the runtime client interface, its fake, the `[sandbox]` values, the check order and the no-widening rule), package 08 (binding guard), package 07 (workspace access), package 03 (maintenance task registry, store) and package 02 (conventions).
- External: an OpenShell gateway, reached through package 44's client.

## Verified External API

- `golang.org/x/net/websocket` v0.61.0, read in the module cache: `type Handler func(*Conn)`; `type Server struct { Config; Handshake func(*Config, *http.Request) error; Handler }` with `func (s Server) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request)`; `func NewConfig(server, origin string) (config *Config, err error)`; `Config.Header http.Header`; `func (config *Config) DialContext(ctx context.Context) (*Conn, error)`; `type Codec struct { Marshal func(v interface{}) (data []byte, payloadType byte, err error); Unmarshal func(data []byte, payloadType byte, v interface{}) (err error) }` with `Send` and `Receive`; `var Message Codec` (a `string` is a text frame, a `[]byte` a binary frame); constants `TextFrame = 1`, `BinaryFrame = 2`. `Handler.ServeHTTP` refuses a request without an `Origin` header; `Server` with a `Handshake` that does not check the origin accepts it.
- `golang.org/x/term` v0.45.0, read in the module cache: `func IsTerminal(fd int) bool`; `func MakeRaw(fd int) (*State, error)`; `func Restore(fd int, oldState *State) error`; `func GetSize(fd int) (width, height int, err error)`.
- `github.com/ai-openshell/sdk-go` (package `openshell/v1`): **unverified**. It is not in the module cache. This package does not call it; the operations of design decision 2 are package 44's.

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Task fork (fork)**: A workspace created from another workspace (its parent) for one task.
- **Sandbox**: An isolated environment in which an agent runs, attached to a workspace (normally a task fork) and started with it checked out. It runs on OpenShell; the hub controls it (§13).
- **OpenShell**: The open-source sandbox runtime Parley's sandboxes run on. It provides the isolation, the policy format and the credential mechanism. The hub is a client of one OpenShell gateway.
- **Profile**: The operator's template for a sandbox, defined in configuration: image, resources, time limits, base policy, credentials and the secrets it exposes.
- **Exposed secret**: A secret (§11) that a profile names in `expose_secrets`. Its real value is placed in the sandbox's environment, where code in the sandbox can read it. Off unless the operator lists the secret (§13).
- **Hub credential**: The fork-bound PAT the hub mints for a sandbox so that it can reach the hub. The workload sees only its placeholder, in `PARLEY_API_KEY`.
- **Bound token**: A PAT confined to one workspace (and the forks created with it).
- **Scope / permission**: A string carried by a PAT that grants read or write access to an area.
- **Session**: An agent session: who ran, on which workspace, with what token usage, and which changes it produced.
- **Agent telemetry**: Run events, tool calls, traces, outcomes and postmortems that agents send to the hub.
- **Main process**: The `command` a sandbox was created with. A sandbox without one is idle and driven by exec.
- **Working directory**: The directory in the sandbox that holds the checkout and that the workload may write.
- **Workload user**: The user the runtime runs the sandbox's processes as.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Gate on every route that uses a sandbox

**Rationale:** A sandbox holds a credential of its creator, so who may act in it, and in which state, must be decided the same way on every route (SBX-FR-010 to SBX-FR-012, §13.3.3).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] IF a request reaches POST …/exec, PUT …/files, GET …/files, GET …/logs or GET …/attach under /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id on a hub whose configuration has no [sandbox] section, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request after authentication and before the scope and workspace checks
   → HTTP 404 with error_type sandboxes_disabled, for an existing and for an unknown workspace slug alike; a request without a credential is still HTTP 401 with error_type unauthenticated
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built without a [sandbox] section and with a temporary store, mounting the route table of internal/sandbox/use.go
   - setup: a user with an API key and one workspace
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/use_test.go, a table over the five route-table entries times slug in {existing, unknown}: r = do(method, path, apiKey); assert r.status == 404 and r.json.error.error_type == 'sandboxes_disabled'; and one row per entry without a credential: assert r.status == 401 and error_type == 'unauthenticated'
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] IF the caller's PAT lacks sandboxes:read on GET …/files or GET …/logs, or lacks sandboxes:write on POST …/exec, PUT …/files or GET …/attach, or the caller lacks read access to the workspace on a read route or write access on a write route, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request without contacting the runtime
   → a PAT without the scope: HTTP 403 with error_type insufficient_scope, whether or not the workspace exists; a caller who cannot see the workspace: HTTP 404 with error_type not_found; a read-only member on exec, PUT …/files or attach: HTTP 403 with error_type forbidden; the fake runtime records no call
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created
   - setup: the route table of internal/sandbox/use.go (five entries: method, path, scope, access level, no-widening flag, allowed states) is mounted with each entry's operation replaced by a probe that records that it was reached and answers 200, so the gate is exercised without the operations behind it
   - setup: the fork's organization has a member M with read-only access to F, and there is a user who is no member
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/use_test.go, a table over (route entry, credential) -> (status, error_type): {each read entry, U's PAT holding sandboxes:write but not sandboxes:read -> 403 insufficient_scope}; {each write entry, U's PAT holding only sandboxes:read -> 403 insufficient_scope}; {each entry, a PAT without the scope on an unknown slug -> 403 insufficient_scope}; {each entry, API key of the non-member -> 404 not_found}; {each write entry, API key of M -> 403 forbidden}; {each read entry, API key of M -> probe reached}: r = do(entry, cred); assert status and error_type; assert the probe was not reached and fakeRuntime.calls == 0 for every refused row
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF the :id of the request is unknown, is not of the form sbx_ plus 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters, or names a sandbox of another workspace, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request as if no such sandbox existed
   → HTTP 404 with error_type sandbox_not_found on each of the five routes
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created
   - setup: the route table of internal/sandbox/use.go (five entries: method, path, scope, access level, no-widening flag, allowed states) is mounted with each entry's operation replaced by a probe that records that it was reached and answers 200, so the gate is exercised without the operations behind it
   - setup: U owns a second workspace with its own sandbox
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/use_test.go, a table over the five entries times id in {'sbx_' + 32 zeros, 'nope', the id of the sandbox of U's other workspace}: r = do(entry with id, U's key); assert r.status == 404 and r.json.error.error_type == 'sandbox_not_found'; assert the probe was not reached
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] IF a caller with write access calls POST …/exec, PUT …/files or GET …/attach with a credential that does not cover the sandbox's hub credential by the no-widening rule of package 44 (a scope of hub_access.scopes it does not hold, or a paths limit narrower than the sandbox's), THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request before validating its body and before looking at the sandbox's state
   → HTTP 403 with error_type insufficient_scope, also when the body is invalid and when the sandbox is stopped; the same credential on GET …/files and GET …/logs is not refused by this rule; the fake runtime records no exec, write or terminal call
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created
   - setup: the route table of internal/sandbox/use.go (five entries: method, path, scope, access level, no-widening flag, allowed states) is mounted with each entry's operation replaced by a probe that records that it was reached and answers 200, so the gate is exercised without the operations behind it
   - setup: S's hub_access.scopes holds git:write; PAT W of U holds sandboxes:write and sandboxes:read but not git:write
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/use_test.go, a table over the three write entries (exec, put files, attach) times S.state in {ready, stopped} with PAT W: r = do(entry, W); assert r.status == 403 and error_type == 'insufficient_scope' and the probe was not reached; then with PAT W on the two read entries (get files, logs): assert the probe was reached; and with U's API key on the write entries with S ready: assert the probe was reached
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] IF a request passes every earlier check and the sandbox's state is not one the route allows: ready for exec, PUT …/files and attach; ready, completed or failed for GET …/files, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request without contacting the runtime
   → HTTP 409 with error_type sandbox_not_ready; exec, PUT …/files and attach are refused in provisioning, stopped, completed, failed and deleted; GET …/files is refused in provisioning, stopped and deleted and answered 200 in completed and failed; the fake runtime records no call for a refused request
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created
   - setup: the route table of internal/sandbox/use.go (five entries: method, path, scope, access level, no-widening flag, allowed states) is mounted with each entry's operation replaced by a probe that records that it was reached and answers 200, so the gate is exercised without the operations behind it
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/use_test.go, a table over state in {provisioning, ready, stopped, completed, failed, deleted} times the five entries: set S.state in the store; r = do(entry, U's key); refused unless (entry is logs) or (state == ready) or (entry is get files and state in {completed, failed}); for refused rows assert r.status == 409 and error_type == 'sandbox_not_ready' and the probe was not reached; for the other rows assert the probe was reached
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] IF the runtime cannot be reached, or returns a failure, while parleyd serves an exec before its first output, a file transfer before its first byte, or the opening of an attach terminal, THEN THE parleyd SHALL answer with the runtime-error answer of package 44, its message being the runtime's text after the scrubbing function of package 45 replaced the sandbox's secret values and cut it to 1,024 bytes
   → HTTP 502 with error_type sandbox_runtime_error; error.message holds the runtime's text with every secret value of the sandbox replaced by [redacted] and is at most 1,024 bytes; neither the response nor the hub's log holds a secret value; a runtime result of kind unsupported is answered the same way
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created
   - setup: the route table of internal/sandbox/use.go is mounted with the operations of exec, put files, get files and attach replaced by a probe that returns the runtime failure errors.New('boom tok_SECRETVALUE') through the runtime-error answer of package 44
   - setup: tok_SECRETVALUE is the value of an exposed secret of S, known to the scrubbing function of package 45; the hub's log is captured
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/use_test.go, a table over the four entries: r = do(entry, U's key); assert r.status == 502 and error_type == 'sandbox_runtime_error'; assert r.json.error.message contains 'boom' and '[redacted]' and not 'tok_SECRETVALUE'; assert the captured log does not hold 'tok_SECRETVALUE'
   ```
1. [REQ-1.7] THE parleyd SHALL for any request to one of the five routes that fails more than one check, answer with the failure of the first check in this order: authentication, sandboxes enabled, binding guard, PAT scope, workspace access, sandbox lookup, no-widening, request validation, sandbox state
   → the status and error_type of the earliest failing check in that order
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created
   - setup: the route table of internal/sandbox/use.go (five entries: method, path, scope, access level, no-widening flag, allowed states) is mounted with each entry's operation replaced by a probe that records that it was reached and answers 200, so the gate is exercised without the operations behind it
   - setup: the validation of the exec entry is the real exec body validation or, until it exists, a probe validation that refuses an empty body with 400 invalid_request
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/use_test.go, a table of POST …/exec requests that each fail two checks -> expected: {PAT without sandboxes:write on a workspace it cannot see -> 403 insufficient_scope}; {the non-member's key with an unknown sandbox id -> 404 not_found}; {U's key, unknown sandbox id, empty body -> 404 sandbox_not_found}; {PAT W of the no-widening test, empty body -> 403 insufficient_scope}; {U's key, empty body, S stopped -> 400 invalid_request}; {a token bound to another workspace and without sandboxes:write -> the binding guard's answer of package 08, not insufficient_scope}: assert status and error_type
   ```

### REQ-2: Run a command and collect its output

**Rationale:** An agent drives an idle sandbox with nothing but HTTP: one request, one command, its exit code and output (SBX-FR-030, SBX-FR-032, SBX-US-03).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN an allowed caller sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/exec with a valid body and no text/event-stream in Accept, for a ready sandbox, THE parleyd SHALL run the command through the runtime as the workload user, in the sandbox's working directory or in workdir when given, with the sandbox's environment overlaid by the request's env, with stdin (or the decoded stdin_base64) written to its standard input and then closed, wait for it to end and answer with its result, whether or not the sandbox's main process is running
   → HTTP 200 with body {exit_code: int, stdout: string, stderr: string, truncated: false, timed_out: false, duration_ms: int >= 0} and no stdout_base64 or stderr_base64 member; a non-zero exit code is answered 200 with that exit_code
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go, a table over (body, fake command behaviour) -> expected: {command ['echo','hi'], prints 'hi\n' exits 0 -> exit_code 0, stdout 'hi\n'}; {exits 3 with stderr 'bad' -> 200, exit_code 3, stderr 'bad'}; {workdir '/tmp', env {A:'1'} -> fake saw dir '/tmp' and env containing A=1 and the sandbox's own variables}; {no workdir -> fake saw the sandbox's working directory}; {env {MODE:'req'} where the sandbox env has MODE=profile -> fake saw MODE=req}; {stdin 'abc' -> fake read 'abc' then EOF}; {stdin_base64 of bytes 00 ff -> fake read those bytes}; {sandbox created with a main command that is still running -> 200}: r = post(exec, body); assert r.status == 200; assert the listed members; assert 'stdout_base64' not in r.json; assert fake ran the command as the workload user
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] IF the exec body has no command, an empty command, a command that is not a list of strings or has more than 256 entries, an env with more than 64 entries or a value over 8192 bytes or a name starting with PARLEY_ or OPENSHELL_ or a name listed in the sandbox's exposed_secrets, both stdin and stdin_base64, a stdin_base64 that is not base64, a stdin over 4194304 bytes after decoding, or a timeout that is not a duration, is zero or exceeds [sandbox].max_exec_timeout; or the body is larger than 8 MiB, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request and run nothing
   → HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_request for each invalid member; HTTP 413 with error_type payload_too_large for a body over 8388608 bytes; the fake runtime records no exec; a command of exactly 256 entries, an env of exactly 64 entries, a stdin of exactly 4194304 bytes and a timeout equal to max_exec_timeout are accepted
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
   - setup: S's exposed_secrets is ['NPM_TOKEN']
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go, a table of bodies -> status: {} -> 400; {command: []} -> 400; {command: 'ls'} -> 400; {command: 257 entries} -> 400; {command: 256 entries} -> 200; {env: 65 entries} -> 400; {env: 64 entries} -> 200; {env: {A: 8193 bytes}} -> 400; {env: {PARLEY_X: '1'}} -> 400; {env: {OPENSHELL_X: '1'}} -> 400; {env: {NPM_TOKEN: 'x'}} -> 400; {stdin and stdin_base64} -> 400; {stdin_base64: '***'} -> 400; {stdin_base64 of 4194305 bytes} -> 400; {stdin_base64 of 4194304 bytes} -> 200; {timeout: 'soon'} -> 400; {timeout: '0s'} -> 400; {timeout: '31m'} -> 400; {timeout: '30m'} -> 200; {body of 8388609 bytes} -> 413 payload_too_large: r = post(exec, body); assert r.status; for 400 rows assert error_type == 'invalid_request' and fakeRuntime.execs unchanged
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] WHEN a collected exec's command is still running when its timeout (default 60 s, or the body's timeout) has passed, THE parleyd SHALL kill the command through the runtime and answer with the output collected until then
   → HTTP 200 with timed_out: true, exit_code: null and the stdout and stderr the command wrote before it was killed; the fake runtime records one kill of that command
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
   - setup: the fake command prints 'partial' and then blocks until killed
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go, a table over timeout in {absent -> 60s, '2s' -> 2s}: start post(exec) in a goroutine; wait until fake reports the command running and its output 'partial' written; clock.Advance(limit - 1s); assert no response yet; clock.Advance(1s); r = response; assert r.status == 200 and r.json.timed_out == true and r.json.exit_code == null and r.json.stdout == 'partial'; assert fake.kills == 1
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] WHEN a collected exec's command writes more than 1048576 bytes to stdout or to stderr, THE parleyd SHALL return the first 1048576 bytes of that stream, cut back to the last complete UTF-8 character, drop the rest and keep reading until the command ends
   → HTTP 200 with truncated: true; the truncated stream's returned bytes are a prefix of what the command wrote and are at most 1048576 bytes; a stream of exactly 1048576 bytes is returned whole with truncated: false; the exit code is the command's
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go, a table over (stdout bytes, stderr bytes) -> (truncated, len stdout, len stderr): {1048576 'a', 0} -> (false, 1048576, 0); {1048577 'a', 0} -> (true, 1048576, 0); {10, 2000000 'b'} -> (true, 10, 1048576); {1048575 'a' + 'é' + 'zz', 0} -> (true, 1048575, 0): r = post(exec); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.truncated and lengths; assert r.json.exit_code == the fake's exit code; assert returned stdout is a prefix of the written bytes
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] WHEN the bytes a collected exec returns for stdout or stderr are not valid UTF-8, THE parleyd SHALL return that stream base64-encoded in stdout_base64 or stderr_base64 with its text member empty, and return the other stream as text
   → HTTP 200 where, for the non-UTF-8 stream, the text member is "" and the _base64 member decodes to exactly the bytes written (up to the 1 MiB cap); the _base64 member of a valid UTF-8 stream is absent
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go: fake command writes bytes ff fe 00 to stdout and 'ok' to stderr; r = post(exec); assert r.json.stdout == '' and base64decode(r.json.stdout_base64) == bytes ff fe 00; assert r.json.stderr == 'ok' and 'stderr_base64' not in r.json; then swapped streams: assert the mirror image
   ```
1. [REQ-2.6] IF the caller's connection closes, or the hub begins to shut down, while a collected exec's command is running, THEN THE parleyd SHALL kill the command through the runtime and release its place in the sandbox's exec count
   → the fake runtime records one kill of that command within 1 second of the disconnect; a following exec in the same sandbox is accepted; the main process of the sandbox is not killed
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
   - setup: the fake command blocks until killed; S has a running main process
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go: ctx, cancel = context with cancel; start post(exec) with ctx in a goroutine against a real httptest.Server; wait until fake reports the command running; cancel(); eventually(1s) fake.kills == 1; assert fake.mainProcessRunning(S); assert post(exec ['true']).status == 200
   ```
1. [REQ-2.7] IF [sandbox].max_concurrent_execs commands started through exec, collected or streamed, are running in the sandbox and another exec request for the same sandbox passes every other check, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the new request and start no command
   → HTTP 429 with error_type rate_limited and no Retry-After header; the fake runtime records no additional exec; an exec in another sandbox is accepted at the same moment
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox].max_concurrent_execs is 2
   - setup: a second ready sandbox S2 on F
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go: start 1 collected and 1 streamed exec in S that block; wait until both run; r = post(exec in S); assert r.status == 429 and error_type == 'rate_limited' and r.header('Retry-After') == ''; assert fake.execs == 2; assert post(exec in S2 ['true']).status == 200; r = post(exec in S with Accept text/event-stream); assert r.status == 429 and Content-Type is application/json
   ```
1. [REQ-2.8] THE parleyd SHALL for any exec that has ended, by exit, timeout, kill after a disconnect, or runtime failure, stop counting it toward the sandbox's exec count, and never count the main process or an attach terminal
   → after an exec ended in any of those ways, a new exec in the same sandbox is answered as if the ended one had never run; with max_concurrent_execs 1, an exec is accepted while the main process runs and an attach terminal is open
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox].max_concurrent_execs is 1
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go, with max_concurrent_execs 1 and S running a main process and one open attach: assert post(exec ['true']).status == 200 (main process and attach do not count); then a table over how the first exec ends {exits 0, exits 9, times out, caller disconnects, fake fails mid-command}: run it to its end; assert the next post(exec ['true']).status == 200
   ```

### REQ-3: Run a command and stream its output

**Rationale:** A long command's output must arrive while it runs and without a size cap (SBX-FR-031).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN an allowed caller sends a valid POST …/exec whose Accept header names text/event-stream, for a ready sandbox, THE parleyd SHALL run the command as for the collected form and send its output as server-sent events while it runs: frames named stdout and stderr in the order the output arrives, each with data {data: string} carrying at most 32768 bytes of output, then exactly one frame named exit, then close the stream
   → HTTP 200 with Content-Type text/event-stream and Cache-Control no-cache; the concatenated data of the stdout frames equals the command's stdout and likewise for stderr; the last frame is event exit with data {exit_code: int, timed_out: false, duration_ms: int}; a frame is received before the command ends when the command wrote output and is still running
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go: fake command writes 'a' to stdout, waits for a signal, writes 'b' to stderr and 100000 bytes 'c' to stdout, exits 4; open post(exec, Accept: text/event-stream) against httptest.Server; assert status 200 and Content-Type starts with 'text/event-stream'; read first frame == (stdout, {data:'a'}) while fake reports the command running; signal; read to end; assert concat(stdout frames) == 'a' + 100000 'c'; assert concat(stderr frames) == 'b'; assert every frame's decoded data <= 32768 bytes; assert last frame == (exit, {exit_code: 4, timed_out: false}) with duration_ms present; assert the body ends after it
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] THE parleyd SHALL for any amount of output of a streamed exec, deliver every byte of stdout and stderr in frames, with no cap and no truncated member
   → the bytes reassembled from the stdout frames equal the bytes the command wrote to stdout, and likewise for stderr, for outputs larger than 1 MiB; no frame carries a truncated member
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go: fake command writes 3 MiB of a repeating pattern to stdout and 2 MiB to stderr; read the stream; assert sha256(concat(stdout frames)) == sha256(written stdout) and the same for stderr; assert the exit frame's data has no 'truncated' member
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] WHEN a chunk of a streamed exec's output is not valid UTF-8, THE parleyd SHALL send that chunk in a frame whose data is {data_base64: string} and keep sending valid chunks as {data: string}
   → the bytes obtained by decoding data_base64 frames and taking data frames as UTF-8, concatenated in order per stream, equal the bytes the command wrote
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; [sandbox] has max_exec_timeout 30m and max_concurrent_execs 8
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/exec_test.go: fake command writes 'ok' then (after a flush) bytes ff 00 fe then 'done' as separate chunks to stdout; read frames; assert the frame for the middle chunk has data_base64 and no data; assert reassembled bytes == 'ok' + ff 00 fe + 'done'
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] WHEN a streamed exec's command is still running when its timeout has passed, THE parleyd SHALL kill the command through the runtime, send the exit frame and close the stream

### REQ-8: Attach an interactive terminal

**Rationale:** A person inspects a running agent from a shell of their own, and leaving ends only that shell (SBX-FR-035).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-8.1] WHEN an allowed caller sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/sandboxes/:id/attach as a WebSocket upgrade for a ready sandbox, THE parleyd SHALL accept the upgrade and start, through the runtime, a new shell /bin/sh as the workload user in the working directory with the sandbox's environment, on a terminal of cols by rows, 80 by 24 when absent
   → the handshake completes with HTTP 101; the fake runtime records one terminal for the sandbox with command /bin/sh, the working directory, the sandbox's environment and the requested size; a handshake without an Origin header is accepted
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; the handler is served by httptest.Server; the test dials with golang.org/x/net/websocket, sending the Authorization header in Config.Header; the fake runtime's terminal echoes what it receives and records resizes
   ```
   in internal/sandbox/attach_test.go, a table over query -> size: {} -> (80, 24); {cols=120&rows=40} -> (120, 40); {cols=1&rows=1000} -> (1, 1000): ws = dial(attach?query) without Origin; assert no error; t = fake.terminals(S)[last]; assert t.command == ['/bin/sh'] and t.dir == S's working directory and t.cols, t.rows == size and t.env contains PARLEY_SANDBOX_ID; ws.Close()
   ```
1. [REQ-8.2] WHILE an attach connection is open, THE parleyd SHALL write the payload of every binary frame from the caller to the terminal's input, and send every chunk of the terminal's output to the caller as one binary frame
   → bytes sent by the caller reach the terminal unchanged, including bytes that are not UTF-8; bytes the terminal writes arrive at the caller in order in binary frames
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub handler under httptest built with the fake runtime of package 44, a temporary store and a test clock; a fork F owned by user U with a sandbox S in state ready that U's API key created; the handler is served by httptest.Server; the test dials with golang.org/x/net/websocket, sending the Authorization header in Config.Header; the fake runtime's terminal echoes what it receives and records resizes

1. [REQ-8.3] WHEN the caller sends a text frame on an attach connection, THE parleyd SHALL resize the terminal to the given size when the frame is the JSON object {resize: {cols, rows}} with both values from 1 to 1000, and ignore any other text frame without closing the connection
   → the fake runtime records a resize to (cols, rows) for a valid frame and none for another text frame; the connection stays usable after an ignored frame

1. [REQ-8.4] WHEN the caller closes an attach connection, or the hub begins to shut down while it is open, THE parleyd SHALL end the shell of that connection through the runtime and nothing else

   → last_activity_at equals the clock's time at open; after a frame that arrives 60 seconds or more after the last write it equals the time of that frame; after close it equals the time of the close; frames within 60 seconds of the last write cause no store write

### REQ-10: CLI commands that use a sandbox

**Rationale:** A person and a script use the same routes from a shell, and a script branches on the command's own exit code (§13.6, SBX-US-03, SBX-US-04).

   → stdout holds exactly the command's stdout bytes and stderr exactly its stderr bytes (data_base64 frames decoded), with nothing added; the exit status is the exit code for 0 to 125 and 125 for a larger one

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: An agent uploads a script, runs it and downloads its result

1. **agent** sends PUT /api/v1/workspaces/<fork>/sandboxes/<id>/files?path=run.sh&mode=755 with a script as the body, using the API key that created the sandbox
2. **parleyd** passes the gate (scope, write access, sandbox found, no widening, state ready), resolves run.sh inside the working directory and writes the file through the runtime client
3. **OpenShell gateway** stores the file in the sandbox's working directory
4. **agent** sends POST …/exec with command ['sh', 'run.sh']
5. **parleyd** takes an exec slot, runs the command through the runtime client, collects its output and answers 200 with exit_code, stdout and stderr
6. **OpenShell gateway** runs the command as the workload user in the working directory; the script writes result.txt
7. **agent** sends GET …/files?path=result.txt and receives the file's bytes
8. **parleyd** has set the sandbox's last_activity_at at each operation and has told the operation observers about one upload, one exec and one download

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the hub started in-process by parleyd's run function on 127.0.0.1:0 with its real router, middleware, authentication and workspace access, the sandbox component of internal/sandbox with the gate, exec, files and activity code of this package, the SQLite store on disk

**Setup:**

- the OpenShell gateway is replaced by the fake runtime of package 44, the only stub
- a user with an API key, a workspace, a fork and a sandbox on it that reached ready
- a recording operation observer is registered
- the sandbox's last_activity_at is noted as T

**End state:**

- the exec answer has exit_code 0 and the stdout the script printed
- the downloaded bytes equal what the script wrote to result.txt
- GET …/sandboxes/<id> shows last_activity_at later than or equal to T and equal to the time of the download
- the observer holds exactly three records: upload, exec with result ok, download

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/sandbox_use_test.go: put(files?path=run.sh&mode=755, 'echo hello; echo data > result.txt'); r = post(exec, {command: ['sh','run.sh']}); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.exit_code == 0 and r.json.stdout == 'hello\n'; b = get(files?path=result.txt); assert b.body == 'data\n'; s = get(sandbox); assert s.json.last_activity_at >= T; assert kinds(observer.records) == ['upload','exec','download']
```

### PATH-2: A developer runs a command with the CLI and gets its exit code

1. **developer** runs parley sandbox exec <fork> <id> -- sh -c 'echo out; echo err >&2; exit 3'
2. **parley CLI** sends POST …/exec with Accept: text/event-stream and the command
3. **parleyd** passes the gate, starts the command through the runtime client and relays its output as stdout and stderr frames, then the exit frame
4. **OpenShell gateway** runs the command and streams its output and exit code
5. **parley CLI** writes 'out' to stdout and 'err' to stderr and exits with status 3

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the parley CLI run through the run function of internal/cli with its real HTTP client, the hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its real router and middleware, the sandbox component with the streamed exec of this package, the SQLite store on disk

**Setup:**

- the OpenShell gateway is replaced by the fake runtime of package 44, the only stub
- a fork with a ready sandbox created by the developer's API key

**End state:**

- the CLI's stdout is 'out\n' and its stderr is 'err\n'
- the CLI's exit status is 3
- no exec is counted as running in the sandbox afterwards

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/sandbox_use_test.go: code = cli.Run(ctx, ['sandbox','exec',fork,id,'--','sh','-c','echo out; echo err >&2; exit 3'], stdout, stderr); assert code == 3; assert stdout == 'out\n' and stderr == 'err\n'
```

### PATH-3: A developer reads the redacted logs of a detached agent

1. **OpenShell gateway** delivers a line the sandbox's main process printed, containing the value of an exposed secret, and a policy log entry for a denied connection
2. **parleyd** the log collector, which found the sandbox ready, stores both lines, the process line with [redacted] in place of the value, and sets last_activity_at for the process line
3. **developer** runs parley sandbox logs <fork> <id>
4. **parley CLI** calls GET …/logs, follows next_cursor to the last page and prints one JSON object per line
5. **parleyd** answers each page from its own store without calling the runtime

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with the log collector running, the log store in the SQLite store on disk, the parley CLI run through the run function of internal/cli

**Setup:**

- the OpenShell gateway is replaced by the fake runtime of package 44, the only stub
- a profile that exposes the secret NPM_TOKEN with value npm_LONGSECRET1; a ready sandbox of that profile with a main process

**End state:**

- the CLI printed two lines: a process line whose text has [redacted] and not npm_LONGSECRET1, and a policy line with action deny, host and port
- the CLI's exit status is 0
- the sandbox's last_activity_at is the time the process line was stored

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/sandbox_use_test.go: fake.emitProcess(id, stdout, 'key npm_LONGSECRET1\n'); fake.emitPolicy(id, deny example.com:443); eventually: code = cli.Run(['sandbox','logs',fork,id]); lines = jsonLines(stdout); assert code == 0 and len(lines) == 2; assert lines[0].line == 'key [redacted]' and lines[1].action == 'deny' and lines[1].host == 'example.com'; assert 'npm_LONGSECRET1' not in stdout
```

### PATH-4: A developer attaches a terminal and leaves without ending the sandbox

1. **developer** opens GET …/attach?cols=100&rows=30 as a WebSocket with an API key that covers the sandbox's hub credential
2. **parleyd** passes the gate, asks the runtime client for a terminal running /bin/sh of 100 by 30, completes the upgrade and sets last_activity_at
3. **OpenShell gateway** starts the shell in the sandbox
4. **developer** sends 'echo hi' in a binary frame and receives the shell's output in binary frames, then closes the connection
5. **parleyd** ends that shell through the runtime client, leaves the sandbox ready and tells the operation observers about one attach

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its real router and middleware, the attach handler of this package over golang.org/x/net/websocket, the SQLite store on disk

**Setup:**

- the OpenShell gateway is replaced by the fake runtime of package 44, the only stub, whose terminal echoes its input
- a fork with a ready sandbox that has a running main process
- a recording operation observer is registered

**End state:**

- the developer received the bytes sent
- after the close the fake runtime shows the terminal closed and the main process running
- GET …/sandboxes/<id> shows state ready
- the observer holds one attach record

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/sandbox_use_test.go: ws = dial(attach?cols=100&rows=30, Authorization); send binary 'echo hi\n'; assert recv == 'echo hi\n'; ws.Close(); eventually fake.terminals(id)[0].closed; assert fake.terminals(id)[0].cols == 100; assert fake.mainProcessRunning(id); assert get(sandbox).json.state == 'ready'; assert kinds(observer.records) == ['attach']
```

## Dependencies

- `45` — provides the sandbox record (state, hub_access, exposed secrets, working directory, environment, last_activity_at) and, through package 44, the runtime client with its named operations, its fake, the [sandbox] limits, the no-widening rule, the runtime-error answer and the metrics recorder that the routes here use; registers a purge hook with its hook list
- `09` — provides the CLI's HTTP client, output and exit codes that the five parley sandbox commands are built on

## Tasks

### 1. Gate the five routes that use a sandbox (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the gate behaviours to internal/sandbox/use_test.go, driving the route table through probe operations as the checks describe, and confirm they fail
- 1.2 Create internal/sandbox/use.go with the route table of this package: POST exec, PUT files, GET files, GET logs and GET attach under /workspaces/{slug}/sandboxes/{id}, each entry with its scope (sandboxes:read for GET files and GET logs, sandboxes:write for the others), its access level (read or write), whether the no-widening rule applies (exec, PUT files, attach), its allowed states (ready; ready, completed and failed for GET files; every state for logs) and its operation
- 1.3 Write the gate that runs before an entry's operation, in this order after the conventions of package 02 have run steps 1 to 4: sandboxes enabled (404 sandboxes_disabled, through package 44's feature check), the binding guard of package 08, the PAT scope, the workspace access rule of package 07, the sandbox lookup through package 45's record (404 sandbox_not_found for an id of the wrong form, an unknown id, or a sandbox whose workspace is not :slug), the no-widening rule of package 44 against the record's hub_access, the entry's validation, and the state check (409 sandbox_not_ready)
- 1.4 Use the existing helpers of packages 02, 07, 08, 44 and 45 for each of those checks; add no second implementation of any of them
- 1.5 Hand the operation a context that holds the caller, the workspace and the sandbox record, so that no operation looks them up again
- 1.6 Answer runtime failures, the kind unsupported included, with the runtime-error answer of package 44 (502 sandbox_runtime_error), giving it the runtime's text after the scrubbing function of package 45 for the sandbox; write no second error answer
- 1.7 Allow each entry to state its own body limit and accepted content types to the conventions of package 02 (exec: JSON up to 8 MiB; PUT files: application/octet-stream and application/x-tar without the default body limit)
- 1.8 Register the route table with the router where package 45 registers the sandbox routes, so the five routes exist only through the gate; the operations are filled in by the tasks that follow

**Touches:**

- `internal/sandbox/use.go`
- `internal/sandbox/use_test.go`
- `internal/hub/`

### 2. Run a command and answer with its collected output (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2

**Steps:**

- 2.1 Add the collected-exec behaviours to internal/sandbox/exec_test.go and confirm they fail
- 2.2 Run commands with ExecStream of package 44's runtime client (argument list, working directory, environment, stdin reader; stdout and stderr as they are produced; the exit code; the command killed when the context ends); add nothing to the interface, its OpenShell implementation or its fake
- 2.3 Validate the body in the gate's validation step: command (1 to 256 strings); env with the validator package 45 uses for the create request (at most 64 entries, values up to 8192 bytes, no PARLEY_ or OPENSHELL_ prefix) plus a refusal of names in the sandbox's exposed_secrets; stdin or stdin_base64 but not both, at most 4194304 bytes decoded; timeout as a duration above zero and at most [sandbox].max_exec_timeout, default 60s
- 2.4 Keep an in-memory count of running execs per sandbox id; take a slot after validation and state, answer 429 rate_limited without Retry-After when [sandbox].max_concurrent_execs slots are taken, and release the slot when the exec ends in any way
- 2.5 Run the command with the sandbox's environment overlaid by the request's env, in workdir or the sandbox's working directory, under a context that ends at the timeout (measured with the replaceable clock) and when the request's context ends
- 2.6 Collect stdout and stderr up to 1048576 bytes each, discard the rest while still draining the command, and set truncated when either stream lost bytes; cut a truncated stream back to the last complete UTF-8 character
- 2.7 Answer 200 with exit_code, stdout, stderr, truncated, timed_out and duration_ms; return a stream that is not valid UTF-8 in its _base64 member with an empty text member; on timeout answer timed_out true with exit_code null and the output so far
- 2.8 When the request's context ends before the command does, kill the command and write no response; when the runtime fails, use the runtime error answer of the gate
- 2.9 Wire the operation into the exec entry of the route table for requests whose Accept does not name text/event-stream

**Touches:**

- `internal/sandbox/exec_test.go`

### 3. Stream a command's output as server-sent events (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3

**Steps:**

- 3.1 Add the streamed-exec behaviours to internal/sandbox/exec_test.go and confirm they fail
- 3.2 Choose the streamed form when the request's Accept header names text/event-stream; validation, the exec slot, the environment, the working directory and the timeout are the code of the collected form, so every refusal is the same JSON error envelope
- 3.3 After the command started, send status 200 with Content-Type text/event-stream and Cache-Control no-cache, and flush after every frame
- 3.4 Send each chunk of output as a frame named stdout or stderr, split so that no frame carries more than 32768 bytes, with data {data} when the chunk is valid UTF-8 and {data_base64} otherwise; apply no cap
- 3.5 When the command ends send one frame named exit with exit_code, timed_out and duration_ms and end the response; on timeout kill the command and send exit with exit_code null and timed_out true
- 3.6 When the request's context ends first, kill the command; when the runtime fails after the headers were sent, end the response without an exit frame; release the exec slot in every case

### 4. Upload a file or a tar stream (implement)

- 4.3 Write the path resolver: join a relative path with the working directory constant of package 45 (/workspace), clean . and .. lexically, and report path_outside_workdir (400) unless the result is the working directory or below it; it follows no symbolic links
- 4.4 Validate the query in the gate's validation step: path present and non-empty and inside the working directory; archive absent or tar; mode an octal number from 0000 to 0777 and absent with archive=tar; content type application/octet-stream, or application/x-tar with archive=tar, else 415

- 4.8 Map a runtime failure to the runtime error answer of the gate and wire the operation into the PUT files entry

**Criteria:** REQ-5

**Steps:**

- 5.2 Use Stat (file or directory, size and mode), Download and Walk of package 44's runtime client; its result of kind not found, for the path or for the working directory, is the missing-path case and every other failure a runtime failure
- 5.3 Validate the query with the path resolver of the upload: path present and inside the working directory, archive absent or tar
- 5.4 Answer 404 path_not_found for a missing path or a missing working directory, and 400 path_is_directory for a directory without archive=tar
- 5.5 File without archive: answer 413 payload_too_large when its size exceeds [sandbox].max_transfer_size; otherwise send 200 with Content-Type application/octet-stream, the Content-Length and the bytes as they are read
- 5.6 archive=tar: send 200 with Content-Type application/x-tar and write a tar stream with archive/tar, one entry per directory and regular file with names relative to the directory and the files' modes, or one entry named by the base name for a file
- 5.7 Count the bytes sent of a tar stream and, at the limit, abort the connection so the caller's read ends with an error and not with a clean end of body
- 5.8 Wire the operation into the GET files entry

- `internal/sandbox/files.go`
- `internal/sandbox/files_test.go`
- `internal/sandbox/use.go`

### 6. Collect, redact and retain each sandbox's logs (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-6

**Depends on:** 1

**Steps:**

- 6.1 Add the collection and retention behaviours to internal/sandbox/logs_test.go and confirm they fail
- 6.2 Add a table for log lines through the migration mechanism of internal/store: a per-row sequence that gives the storage order, the sandbox id, time (whole seconds, UTC), source, stream, line, and for policy lines action, program, host, port and credential
- 6.3 Follow a sandbox with Logs of package 44's runtime client, one stream with source process and one with source policy, each with follow and since, until the context ends; the fake emits the entries a test gives it
- 6.4 Write the collector: every 5 seconds on the replaceable clock it reads the sandboxes in state ready from the store, starts one follower for each that has none and cancels the followers of sandboxes that are no longer ready; it starts with the hub when sandboxes are enabled and stops at shutdown
- 6.5 A follower asks the runtime for output from the time of the sandbox's last stored line, skips the lines of that second that are already stored, and ends when its stream breaks, so that the next round opens it again
- 6.6 Split process output into lines at line ends, holding an unfinished line until its end arrives, and split a line longer than 16384 bytes into consecutive lines of at most 16384 bytes
- 6.7 Before storing, replace every exact match of each exposed secret value of the sandbox that is at least 8 characters long with [redacted]; take the values from the sandbox component of package 45 and keep them out of the store and the log
- 6.8 Store policy entries with source policy, stream null, their text and their action, program, host, port and, when present, the provider name as credential
- 6.9 Register one task in the maintenance registry of package 03 that deletes lines older than [sandbox].log_retention and lines whose sandbox record no longer exists, and register a purge hook with the list of package 45 that deletes a sandbox's lines in the transaction that removes its record
- 6.10 Start the collector and register the maintenance task in the hub's composition

- `internal/sandbox/logs_store.go`
- `internal/sandbox/logs_collect.go`
- `internal/sandbox/logs_test.go`

- `internal/hub/`

### 7. Serve a sandbox's logs as pages and as a followed stream (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-7

**Steps:**

- 7.1 Add the read and follow behaviours to internal/sandbox/logs_test.go and confirm they fail
- 7.2 Validate the query in the gate's validation step: source process or policy; since an RFC 3339 timestamp; tail an integer of at least 1; follow true or false; follow=true not together with cursor or limit; limit and cursor by the list helper of package 02
- 7.3 Paged read: select the sandbox's lines by source and since, restrict to the last tail lines of that selection when tail is given, order by storage sequence, and answer {items, next_cursor} through the list helper of package 02; never call the runtime
- 7.4 Render an item as {time, source, stream, line}, with action, program, host and port for policy lines and credential only when it is set
- 7.5 Follow: send 200 with Content-Type text/event-stream and Cache-Control no-cache, one frame named log per selected stored line, then each newly stored matching line within 1 second, found by reading the store past the last sequence sent when the collector signals new lines or after at most 1 second
- 7.6 End a followed stream when the request's context ends, when the hub shuts down, or when the sandbox's state is deleted, after sending the lines stored until then
- 7.7 Wire the operation into the logs entry of the route table

### 10. Add parley sandbox exec (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-10.1, REQ-10.2, REQ-10.3, REQ-10.4

- 10.3 Build the body: command; workdir, env and timeout only when their flags were given; with --stdin read standard input to its end, refuse more than 4194304 bytes with a client_error before any request, and send it as stdin_base64
- 10.4 Send the request through the client of package 09 without the 30-second timeout, as a raw response the command reads itself; a non-2xx answer is the hub's envelope on stderr and exit status 1, as for every command
- 10.5 Default form: send Accept: text/event-stream, parse the frames, write stdout frames to stdout and stderr frames to stderr (decoding data_base64) as they arrive, and take the exit status from the exit frame
- 10.6 With --json: send no text/event-stream, print the response document through the output of package 09 and take the exit status from exit_code and timed_out
- 10.7 Exit with the command's exit code, mapping values above 125 to 125; on timed_out report wait_timeout on stderr and exit 1; when the stream ends without an exit frame report client_error and exit 2
